knowledge:
- key_parameters: bind=The length of the binding region in base pairs (e.g., 147 for nucleosomes) ;; support=The length of the support regions flanking the binding region ;; chrLen=The length of the chromosome, required for piling up reads ;; extend=The number of base pairs to extend each read during pileup ;; plot=Logical value indicating whether to generate diagnostic plots during processing ;; bgCutoff=Limits the change in background estimate for adjacent windows, chosen between 0.5 and 1 (lower is more restrictive) ;; supCutoff=Limits the change in support region estimates, chosen between 0.5 and 1 ;; digits=Number of decimal places to round binding site scores for compression (default is 16) ;; compress=Logical value indicating whether to compress read counts using run-length encoding ;; sub=Logical value indicating whether peaks can be separated by a relatively low scoring region even if the score does not drop below the threshold
- alternatives: ShortRead=Used to read real mapped reads into an AlignedRead object before passing to ChIPseqR ;; ChIPsim=Used for sophisticated simulation of ChIP-seq data instead of the simple simulation shown in the vignette
- when_to_use: Use this package for high-resolution analysis of end-sequenced nucleosomes after MNase digest, nucleosome positioning, histone modification experiments, or other transcription factor ChIP-seq experiments where binding and support region lengths can be estimated.
- pitfalls: Low coverage and high noise levels can lead to missing binding sites or overlapping predictions representing alternative positions ;; getBindLen parameter estimation assumes symmetric read count distribution in support regions and regularly spaced binding sites, which may fail for non-nucleosome proteins ;; Overestimating the variance of the null distribution can result in conservative p-values ;; Run-length encoding compression (compress = TRUE) can occasionally increase memory usage for some datasets, in which case compress = FALSE should be used.

workflows.name: nucleosome_calling_and_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify nucleosome positioning and binding sites from mapped ChIP-seq reads, estimate parameters, and visualize results.
input: reads.csv (a data frame or AlignedRead object containing chromosome, position, length, and strand of mapped reads)
workflows.stages: 1. Pile up reads to count strand-specific coverage using strandPileup ;; 2. Estimate binding and support region lengths using getBindLen ;; 3. Call nucleosomes and identify binding sites using simpleNucCall ;; 4. Plot diagnostic distributions to assess the null model ;; 5. Extract predicted peaks and filter overlapping predictions ;; 6. Visualize read counts and predicted binding sites in a genomic window ;; 7. Decompress data if needed for downstream analysis
workflows.code:
counts <- strandPileup(reads, chrLen=2e6, extend=1, plot=FALSE)
bLen <- getBindLen(counts, bind = c(100,200), support = c(5, 50))
nucs <- simpleNucCall(counts, bind=147, support=15, plot=FALSE)
plot(nucs, type="density")
plot(nucs, type="qqplot")
predicted <- peaks(nucs)[[1]][911]
plot(counts, chr="chr1", center=predicted, score=nucs, width=1000, type="window")
abline(v=pos[pos < predicted + 1000 & pos > predicted - 1000], col=3, lty=3)
calls <- peaks(nucs)[[1]][c(1,which(diff(peaks(nucs)[[1]]) >= 170)+1)]
length(calls)
counts2 <- decompress(counts)
